$comment: The standards GlideComp follows, and how to tell when one moves. Read by web/scripts/standards-check.ts and the monthly routine .claude/commands/standards-check.md. `follows` is what the tree implements; `seen` is what the last run saw (written by --record). See docs/standards/review-log.md.

standards.name: FAI Sporting Code Section 7F: XC Scoring (CIVL GAP)

queries: FAI Sporting Code Section 7F XC Scoring {next} edition
Sporting Code S7F XC Scoring {year} V1.1
FAI CIVL {year} edition of Section 7 published

standards.onChange: Owner, always. A new edition (effective 1 May) or errata is a scoring decision: which comps it applies to and from when. It needs a transcription under docs/reference/ (follow fai-s7f-xc-scoring-2024/INGESTION.md and extract_s7f.py), a note in web/engine/scoring-changes/ measured over the archive, and the owner's go-ahead. Raise an issue with the edition's red-marked changes summarised and the engine files each touches. Edition-coupled data to regenerate with a new edition: SpecRef.astro's SPEC_DESTS (section to PDF page), the PDF links in gap-types.ts, gap-scoring.ts, /scoring/gap and /about, the rules_edition payload value and the label in rules-edition.ts, and every § citation (docs/2026-08-09-s7f-2026-migration-plan.md has the renumbering table from the last migration).

standards.name: FAI Sporting Code Section 7A: General (hang gliding and paragliding)
standards.follows: not pinned: /scoring/track-validity links the 2025 edition, /scoring/gap the 2022 one

queries: FAI Sporting Code Section 7A {year} changes track log verification

standards.onChange: Owner. GlideComp relies on S7A §4.4.2 and §4.4.6 (track-log verification and the organiser override), §5.2.5.1 (FTV discard factor) and §5.2.5.4 (tied ranks). A change to those can change which tracks are scored or how comps total; raise an issue naming the clauses that moved and the code they touch. Pointing both pages' S7A links at the same, current PDF is a safe link fix when the clauses they cite didn't move.

standards.name: IGC flight recorder file format (FAI IGC technical specification)
standards.follows: IGC file format as documented in 2008 (igc-parser.ts cites the xp-soaring mirror); the FAI specification it belongs to was at the 2024 edition with AL9 when the register was written

queries: FAI IGC technical specification GNSS flight recorder {year} amendment
IGC file format specification new edition {year}

standards.onChange: Owner if the record formats the parser reads change (A, H, I, B, C, E, G records, time or date fields). A new optional record type the parser can ignore is worth a log line only.

standards.name: XCTrack task format (.xctsk v1, QR v2)
standards.follows: task file v1 and QR code v2
standards.onChange: Read the snapshot diff. A new optional field or a clarification is safe to PR with a parser test. Anything that changes how a task's geometry, start gates or goal is read changes scores: owner, with a scoring-changes note.

standards.name: Model Context Protocol
standards.onChange: Owner. The revisions the endpoint speaks come from @modelcontextprotocol/server's SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS (the card advertises the same list), so adopting a new revision is an SDK upgrade plus a read of the revision's changelog (transport, auth, tool annotations). Raise an issue; coordinate with the dependency routine.

standards.name: MCP Server Card (SEP-2127) schema
standards.onChange: Safe to PR if the card still validates: replace the vendored schema with upstream, run `bun test web/workers/mcp-api`, and adjust cardFor() only for a new optional field. A new required field, a removed field the card uses, or a changed $schema URL (a v2 schema) is a major change: owner.

standards.name: Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD) specification
standards.onChange: Safe to PR for a minor version whose changes are optional fields, recommendations or wording, provided ard.json still validates against the refreshed schema (ard-schema). A changed well-known path, link relation, required field or identifier format is a major change: owner.

standards.name: ARD entry and manifest JSON Schema
standards.onChange: Safe to PR if ard.json still validates: replace the vendored schema and run `bun test web/workers/mcp-api`. If it no longer validates, the fix to ard.json is safe only when it is mechanical (a renamed or newly required field we can fill from what the file already says); otherwise owner.

standards.name: AI Catalog specification
standards.onChange: Read the snapshot diff. Safe to PR for editorial changes and new optional members. A new specVersion, a renamed or required member, or a changed well-known path or media type: update ai-catalog.json and the discovery test if mechanical, otherwise owner.

standards.name: MCP Server Card discovery (ext-server-card docs/discovery.md)
standards.onChange: Read the snapshot diff. Card location, required headers (CORS, cache, ETag), media types and the catalog's path are what we implement. A mechanical change to headers or media types is safe to PR with its test; a moved card location or catalog path is the owner's call.

standards.name: llms.txt format
standards.onChange: Read the snapshot diff. A format rule change (sections, link lists, the Optional section) is safe to PR: reshape llms.txt and the llms.txt test together, keeping its words. New wording addressed to people is the owner's.

standards.name: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines
standards.onChange: Owner. A new WCAG Recommendation is a policy decision for docs/accessibility-standard.md and CLAUDE.md, not a code change. Raise an issue summarising the new success criteria and which surfaces they'd touch.

standards.name: OAuth 2.1 (IETF draft draft-ietf-oauth-v2-1)
standards.onChange: Owner, but usually informational: `follows` is the draft revision the MCP authorisation spec we implement (2025-11-25) cites, and the provider itself is Better Auth's mcp() plugin. A newer draft is a log line until the MCP spec adopts it; publication as an RFC, or a newer MCP revision citing a newer draft, is an issue.

standards.name: RFC 9728 OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata
standards.onChange: `follows: none` means not obsoleted. If an RFC obsoletes it, owner: read what changed for the 401 challenge and the metadata document.

standards.name: RFC 8414 OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata
standards.onChange: `follows: none` means not obsoleted. If an RFC obsoletes it, owner.

standards.onChange: `follows: none` means not obsoleted. If an RFC obsoletes it, owner.
